findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed ice machine in back storage area to be soiled with black residue on the exterior baffles. PIC was informed that the ice machine will need to be cleaned and sanitized. A follow-up will be conducted on July 7th (accomodating for the holiday and weekend) to ensure the machine has been properly cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed tomatoes and lettuce in the kitchen drawer cooler measure 51F with the probe. PIC was informed, and since the items were recently moved to the drawer cooler to the walk-in, the items were returned to the walk-in cooler. This violation is considered corrected on site.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The drawer cooler in the kitchen measured 53F with the infrared and probe thermometers. The digital display on the exterior of the cooler read 43F. The PIC was informed that the cooler was not functioning and the food items inside were moved to the walk-in cooler. This cooler is not adequate for holding time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods until it is repaired. The walk-in cooler will be used until repairs are complete. A follow-up is scheduled for July 7th (accommodating the holiday and weekend) to ensure the cooler has been repaired.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed hand sink in kitchen to be obstructed with paper towels and dish soap in sink basin. Informed PIC of issue, and items were removed from hand sink. Ensure hand sink is easily accessible at all times to promote frequent and proper hand washing. Violation is considered corrected on site.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Observed molded sliced tomato in prep cooler drawer. PIC was informed of unsafe food, and the tomatoes were discarded. To avoid serving unsafe food to the public, ensure cut produce is clearly date marked and discarded after 7 days. Violation is considered corrected on site.
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed sanitizer spray bottle in the kitchen to “bleach out” test strip, indicating that the solution was too potent. PIC was informed that sanitizer was too strong, and the bottle was diluted. Ensure bleach sanitizer solutions are at an appropriate concentration to avoid toxicity. Violation is considered corrected on site.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed soda nozzles at the bar to be soiled. The drainage line and catch tube for the soda nozzles were also soiled and had mold growth. One of the catch tubes were clogged as well. PIC was informed of the issue and plans to use a designated brush to clean the catch tubes. A follow-up will be conducted on 3/20/2025 to ensure the soda nozzles and catch tubes have been cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed produce in prep cooler (tomato, lettuce, onion) and walk-in cooler (salads, creamer, milk) to have no date mark. Informed PIC that time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods that are considered ready-to-eat need to be date marked and discarded after 7 days. A follow-up has been scheduled for 3/20/2025 to ensure date marking compliance.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed hood in kitchen to be soiled dust and grease. Observed chest freezer in back storage area to be soiled with old food (french fries). Informed PIC that chest freezer and hood are in need of a cleaning. Routine cleaning of non-food contact surfaces prevents cross-contamination with food and food-contact surfaces. Ensure that surfaces are clean for next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed floor of walk-in cooler to be soiled with food debris. Informed PIC that floor needed a cleaning. Keeping flooring in the facility clean not only prevents cross-contamination, but can prevent pest infestation as well. Ensure flooring is clean by next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed sanitizing solution in use in kitchen to test at 0 ppm Cl-. New sanitizing solution was made during inspection, and tested at 200 ppm Cl-.

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed interior cavity of kitchen microwave to be soiled with food splash and debris. Clean and sanitize interior cavity of kitchen microwave. 

4-602.12: (A) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking and baking EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours. This section does not apply to hot oil cooking and filtering EQUIPMENT if it is cleaned as specified in Subparagraph 4-602.11(D)(6). (B) The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment: 3-304.12: Observed blade of knife used for food prep to be stored under pizza oven on counter top. Knife was moved during inspection. FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment: 6-305.11: (A) Observed 2 cell phones and Bluetooth speaker on shelf above window in kitchen, located directly over a food contact surface. Phones and speaker were moved during inspection. Dressing rooms or dressing areas shall be designated if EMPLOYEES routinely change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions.

Hand sinks in both restrooms are missing hand washing signs. One is completely absent the other in ripped mostly off of the hand towel dispenser. Hand wash signs were provided to the facility.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor. 
Observed containers of seasoning to be stored on bread crates that are not at least six inches above the floor. Crates are also difficult to clean around and often lead to other issues. Discontinue this practice and provide proper storage for these items.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Observed 3 soda guns at the bar to be soiled. Clean and maintain free of accumulated debris. The soda guns were properly cleaned during inspection. Washed, rinsed and sanitized. 4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment: Observed a box of fries on the floor of the walk in cooler. A bag of raw uncut onions are also observed on the floor in the back storage area. Put food up when it arrives from the truck. Truck was yesterday. 3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment: Observed wet wiping cloth to be stored on the coffin cooler during lunch rush. Cloth was placed back into sanitizer container. 3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment: Observed boxes of single-use articles to be stored on the floor in the facility. 4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: Soda nozzles in the bar area were observed to have an accumulation of mold/soil residue. Ensure these surfaces are soaked and sanitized to prevent the potential contamination of the contact surfaces with the food items being served. Ensure this process is conducted at a frequency that prevents this accumulation.
4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: Overall the facility is in need of a deep clean, especially in hard to reach areas, under equipment, and along the areas where the walls meet the floor int he bar area and back storage area. Ensure these areas are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to prevent the accumulation of food debris and soil residue. This cleaning will also discourage potential pests.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-201.11: Facility did not have employee health reporting agreements on file. A copy was left with the facility and the PIC was making copies during the inspection. These forms shall be available during the next routine inspection and kept on file for display upon inspector request. The employees were signing them today during the inspection.
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC.
